newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rubber industry sees sales rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German rubber industry sees sales rise in 1997.

text.p: German manufacturers of rubber products maintain an earlier forecast for a sales expansion by 2.5 percent in 1997, Guenther Schreck, board member at Frankfurt-based industry association WDK said in a statement.
Sales in 1996 increase by 1.7 percent to 16.42 billion marks.
Schreck said that sales of technical rubber products, such as hoses and seals, which had fallen in the domestic market last year, were now especially encouraging, both at home and abroad.
Tyre sales were also satisfactory, with the car industry accounting for three quarters of all sales.
Replacement tyre sales for private passenger vehicles in Jan-April, for example, were up 6.6 percent from the same 1996 period at 11.7 million units, Schreck said.
Sales revenue in both tyres and technical products lagged growth rates in the tonnage because of global competition, he added.

WDK members were still expecting successful transactions in 1997 because rubber product consuming industries in Germany and neighbouring European countries were reporting improved conditions, with the exception of mining and construction.
The industry last year consumed 452,000 tonnes of which 193,000 tonnes were natural rubber and the rest synthetic.
Schreck's speech was distributed during a conference on rubber technology.
